 Damian Lillard and the Portland Trail Blazers look to bounce back after their first loss against the Utah Jazz.
 The Portland Trail Blazers (3-1) opened the season with three straight wins and are one of the NBA’s surprise teams. Damian Lillard is back from injury, and new addition Ja Morant has made the backcourt work as an All-Star duo. They are looking to bounce back from their first loss of the season. Portland takes the road to play the Utah Jazz (1-4) for the first time. This also kicks off a four-game Western Conference road trip for Portland. In Portland’s first three games, they averaged 128.6 points per game. They were held to just 103 points in the loss. Five players are averaging double-digit scoring for Portland, led by All-Star Deni Avdija.

 Avdija is pacing the offense with 22.8 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 6.5 assists per game. He is coming off an All-Star season leading Portland to the playoffs. Avdija now has two more All-Stars running alongside him in the backcourt in Lillard and Morant.
 Lillard is getting back into All-Star form over four games. He is averaging 18.5 points per game on 35.1% shooting from three. Morant is averaging 15.8 points and 5.5 assists per game on 54.2% shooting.
 Utah has lost three straight games, all by single-digit margins, including an overtime loss to the San Antonio Spurs. This game ends a five-game home stand in which Utah won the first and is trying to avoid losing the final four.
